name: Kybella for neck/jowl

lead: Kybella is the brand name of deoxycholic acid, an injectable the US FDA approved on April 29, 2015 for reducing moderate-to-severe fat below the chin. People after a sharper jawline or neck also discuss it for the jowl area, which is not part of the approved indication.

When injected into submental fat it destroys fat cells, which the body then metabolizes over several months. A generic version became available in the US in April 2021, and a 2025 registered study examined patient satisfaction with combined face and neck treatments including Kybella.

paras: It is a clinic treatment given by a clinician as a series of injections into the fat under the chin, with the reduction showing over the following months. It is sold as Belkyra in some markets such as Australia.

Treatment is clinician-administered and prescription-only. The source reviewed does not detail adverse effects, so patients are referred to the product label and their clinician for the risk profile. Jowl and other neck uses are off-label.

angle.text: Kybella injections destroy fat cells under the chin for a slimmer chin and neck, with the reduction visible after treatment. The FDA approved it in 2015 for submental fat; jowl and neck use is off-label.

lead: Kybella is a prescription injectable form of deoxycholic acid, made by Kythera Biopharmaceuticals and sold as Belkyra in some markets such as Australia.[1] The US FDA approved it on April 29, 2015 for reducing moderate-to-severe fat below the chin, and a generic became available in April 2021.[1]

When injected into submental fat it destroys fat cells, which the body then metabolizes over several months.[1] Using it on the jowls or other neck areas is not part of the US approved indication; this article documents how the topic is discussed rather than recommending it.

paras: The approved US use is reduction of moderate-to-severe fat below the chin.[1] Looksmaxxing discussion extends this to neck and jowl contouring, which is off-label.
Injected deoxycholic acid destroys adipocytes in the treated fat, and the body clears the contents over several months.[1]
Kybella was developed by Kythera Biopharmaceuticals and approved by the FDA on April 29, 2015; a generic followed in April 2021.[1]

A phase 4 trial registered as NCT06783621, completed and enrolling 130 participants from January 2025, assessed patient satisfaction with overall face and neck appearance after combined treatment with onabotulinumtoxinA, Juvederm fillers, Kybella, CoolSculpting Elite and SkinMedica products for facial contouring.[2] Because Kybella was one of several combined treatments, that registration does not isolate its effect.

timeline.event: FDA approves Kybella on April 29 for submental fat.[1]
A generic version becomes available in the US.[1]
Phase 4 combined face and neck contouring study begins.[2]
